option.approach: Retain only order preservation and derive the upper bound η≤1/2 and downward closure of the admissible set. Identify precisely what additional statement would exclude equality without assuming strict order preservation.

options.counterfactual: Every finite AW*-factor satisfying the quasitrace hypotheses in the problem is monotone sequentially complete.
options.approach: Identify a precise monotone sequential completeness theorem and verify its hypotheses against the definition in the problem. Such a theorem would immediately rule out the required absence of a least upper bound.

options.approach: Try to prove that every bounded increasing sequence is Cauchy for the quasitrace metric, then use metric completeness and closure of the positive cone to construct its least upper bound.

options.approach: Investigate a projection-dilation proof of sequential order completeness. Encode positive increments as compressions of orthogonal projections and determine whether their projection join yields the required supremum.

options.counterfactual: There exists a finite AW*-factor satisfying the problem's hypotheses with an increasing sequence of positive contractions whose increments all have the same positive quasitrace and which has no least upper bound.
options.approach: Investigate whether one such witness can be transformed into witnesses for every η<1/2. Scaling supplies smaller increments, while compression to suitable corners might increase the normalized increment.
